channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-lucid-dreams
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: ezscore — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Artifact-aware sleep stage classifiers for forehead EEG headbands such as the ZMax.

item.title: ZMax LD Set — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Research-grade EEG headband that detects REM sleep and plays light, sound and vibration cues, used in lab studies of lucid dream induction.

item.title: Yume Nikki — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Free exploration game set in the strange, dark world inside a girl's dreams.

item.title: YASA — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Python package for sleep analysis, including automatic sleep staging of polysomnography recordings.

item.title: Wake Up, Work on Dreams, Back to Bed and Lucid Dream: A Sleep Laboratory Study (Erlacher, D., & Stumbrys, T. 2020) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Waking participants after six hours to practice MILD for 30 to 60 minutes produced lucid dreams in 36 to 54% of unselected participants, compared with 9% after reading.

item.title: Vanilla Sky — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: A man whose life unravels after a disfiguring accident slowly realizes that the world he inhabits is a lucid dream.

item.title: UCLA Mindful — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Guided exercises on breath, sound, and body awareness.

item.title: UC San Diego Center for Mindfulness — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Guided exercises on mental noting, awareness of breath, and body scan.

item.title: Two-Way Communication in Lucid REM Sleep Dreaming (Baird, B., LaBerge, S., & Tononi, G. 2021) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Commentary on Konkoly et al. 2021 that discusses whether longer two-way conversations with lucid dreamers are feasible.

item.title: TritonSleep — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Private on-device dream journal, reality-check reminders and guided MILD, WBTB, SSILD, WILD and FILD sessions with evidence ratings; no account.

item.title: The Effectiveness of Lucid Dreaming Therapy in Patients With Nightmares: A Systematic Review (Ouchene, R., et al. 2023) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Found 4 randomized controlled trials and several case studies; most reported fewer nightmares in adults, but internal validity was limited.

item.title: The Cognitive Neuroscience of Lucid Dreaming (Baird, B., Mota-Rolim, S. A., & Dresler, M. 2019) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Reviewed EEG, neuroimaging, lesion, drug and brain stimulation studies, finding EEG results mostly underpowered and mixed, prefrontal and parietal regions implicated, and cholinergic stimulation combined with mental set training the most promising induction approach.

item.title: The Clinical Neuroscience of Lucid Dreaming (Tzioridou, S., et al. 2025) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Reviewed links between lucid dreaming and nightmare disorder, depression, anxiety, psychosis and dissociation, and the potential drawbacks of lucid dreaming interventions.

item.title: Targeted Lucidity Reactivation Implemented in an Open-Source watchOS App (Mallela, R., & Mallett, R. 2024) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Developed an open-source iOS/watchOS application that runs targeted lucidity reactivation at home, using Apple Watch motion and heart rate data to time cues to REM sleep.

item.title: TLR — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Open-source iOS/watchOS app for targeted lucidity reactivation, with Apple Watch sleep staging to time cues to REM sleep.

item.title: Superliminal — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: First-person puzzle game about escaping a surreal dream world by bending perspective.

item.title: Sleep and Dream Database — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Kelly Bulkeley's archive of dream reports and survey data for research.

item.title: Reality Testing and the Mnemonic Induction of Lucid Dreams: Findings From the National Australian Lucid Dream Induction Study (Adventure-Heart, D. J., et al. 2017) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Compared reality testing, WBTB and MILD in 169 participants and found that combining all three induced lucid dreams, especially when participants fell asleep soon after practicing MILD.

item.title: Provoking Lucid Dreams at Home With Sensory Cues Paired With Pre-Sleep Cognitive Training (Konkoly, K. R., et al. 2024) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Moved targeted lucidity reactivation (TLR) to a smartphone without polysomnography. Lucid dreaming increased compared with the prior week and with blinded control nights, but only when the sleep cues matched the pre-sleep training sounds.

item.title: Pre-Sleep Treatment With Galantamine Stimulates Lucid Dreaming: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Study (LaBerge, S., LaMarca, K., & Baird, B. 2018) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: In 121 participants combining WBTB and MILD, 4 mg and 8 mg of galantamine, a prescription drug, raised the share reporting a lucid dream to 27% and 42%, compared with 14% on placebo.

item.title: Paller Lab — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Ken Paller's cognitive neuroscience lab at Northwestern University, behind the two-way dream communication and at-home TLR studies.

item.title: Oniri — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Dream journal with voice recording, dream interpretation and lucid dreaming lessons.

item.title: Oniri — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Dream journal with voice recording, dream interpretation and lucid dreaming lessons.

item.title: Neural Correlates of Dream Lucidity Obtained From Contrasting Lucid Versus Non-Lucid REM Sleep: A Combined EEG/fMRI Case Study (Dresler, M., et al. 2012) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: In the one participant (of four) with lucid REM episodes long enough to analyze, lucid dreaming activated the precuneus, parietal lobules, and prefrontal and occipito-temporal cortices compared with non-lucid REM sleep.

item.title: Metacognitive Mechanisms Underlying Lucid Dreaming (Filevich, E., Dresler, M., et al. 2015) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Found greater frontopolar (BA9/10) gray matter volume in people reporting high dream lucidity, and stronger activation of the same region when they monitored their own thoughts while awake.

item.title: Measuring Consciousness in Dreams: The Lucidity and Consciousness in Dreams Scale (Voss, U., et al. 2013) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Developed the LuCiD scale, with eight factors including insight, control, thought, memory and dissociation, now a standard outcome measure in lucid dreaming studies.

item.title: Lucid Scribe — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Dream journal, Homing Signal cue training, guided MILD, SSILD, WBTB and FILD, targeted lucidity reactivation, and REM detection with the INSPEC device.

item.title: Lucid Scribe — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Dream journal, Homing Signal cue training, guided MILD, SSILD, WBTB and FILD, targeted lucidity reactivation, and REM detection with the INSPEC device.

item.title: Lucid Dreaming: Intensity, But Not Frequency, Is Inversely Related to Psychopathology (Aviram, L., & Soffer-Dudek, N. 2018) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: In 187 students, lucid dream frequency was unrelated to psychopathology, while deliberate induction predicted increases in dissociation and schizotypy over two months.

item.title: Lucid Dreaming, Plain and Simple by Robert Waggoner and Caroline McCready — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Short, practical introduction to lucid dreaming techniques and what to do once lucid.

item.title: Lucid Dreaming Treatment for Nightmares: A Pilot Study (Spoormaker, V. I., & van den Bout, J. 2006) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Randomized 23 nightmare sufferers to individual, group or waiting-list conditions; one 2-hour lucid dreaming treatment session reduced nightmare frequency at 12 weeks, but becoming lucid was not necessary for the improvement.

item.title: Lucid Dreaming Occurs in Activated Rapid Eye Movement Sleep, Not a Mixture of Sleep and Wakefulness (Baird, B., Tononi, G., & LaBerge, S. 2022) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Found that signal-verified lucid dreams occur during REM sleep with higher eye movement density, and that the reported 40 Hz "hybrid state" signal was an eye movement artifact.

item.title: Lucid Dreaming Incidence: A Quality Effects Meta-Analysis of 50 Years of Research (Saunders, D. T., et al. 2016) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Estimated that 55% of people have had at least one lucid dream and 23% have them monthly or more.

item.title: Lucid Dream — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: A journalist uses lucid dreaming to search his memories for clues to his son's kidnapping.

item.title: Llewellyn's Complete Book of Lucid Dreaming by Clare R. Johnson — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Comprehensive guide to lucid dreaming techniques and to using lucid dreams for creativity, nightmares and sleep problems.

item.title: Institut für Bewusstseins- und Traumforschung — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Brigitte Holzinger's institute in Vienna, offering research, seminars and lucid dreaming therapy for nightmares.

item.title: Induction of Self Awareness in Dreams Through Frontal Low Current Stimulation of Gamma Activity (Voss, U., et al. 2014) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Reported that 25 and 40 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) during REM sleep induced self-reflective awareness in dreams, while other frequencies did not.

item.title: Inducing Lucid Dreaming With Multisensory Stimulation: A Preregistered Multi-Center Study (Picard-Deland, C., Jafarzadeh Esfahani, M., et al. 2026) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Preprint. Combined pre-sleep SSILD training with light, sound and vibration cues during REM sleep in 60 participants across three labs. Cueing did not make lucid dreams more frequent than sham, but roughly doubled the duration of signal-verified lucid dreams.

item.title: IASD Annual Conference — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Yearly conference of the International Association for the Study of Dreams, with research talks and lucid dreaming workshops.

item.title: Frequent Lucid Dreaming Associated With Increased Functional Connectivity Between Frontopolar Cortex and Temporoparietal Association Areas (Baird, B., et al. 2018) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Found stronger resting-state connectivity between the anterior prefrontal cortex and temporoparietal regions in frequent lucid dreamers, but no differences in brain structure.

item.title: Findings From the International Lucid Dream Induction Study (Adventure-Heart, D. J. 2020) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Compared five combinations of reality testing, WBTB, MILD and SSILD in 355 participants and found MILD and SSILD similarly effective, regardless of prior lucid dreaming experience.

item.title: Electrophysiological Correlates of Lucid Dreaming: Sensor and Source Level Signatures (Demirel, Ç., et al. 2025) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Pooled EEG across labs and found minimal sensor-level differences between lucid and non-lucid REM sleep, but reduced right parietal beta power and more alpha and gamma connectivity during lucid dreaming.

item.title: Effectiveness of Motor Practice in Lucid Dreams: A Comparison With Physical and Mental Practice (Stumbrys, T., Erlacher, D., & Schredl, M. 2016) — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: In 68 participants, practicing finger tapping in a lucid dream improved next-morning performance about as much as physical or waking mental practice.

item.title: Dreams of Awakening by Charlie Morley — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Lucid dreaming and mindfulness of dream and sleep, combining Western techniques with Tibetan Buddhist practice.

item.title: DreamBank — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Searchable collection of more than 20,000 dream reports from research studies and dream journals.

item.title: Dream and Nightmare Laboratory — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Tore Nielsen's lab in Montreal, studying dreams, nightmares and sleep.

item.title: Dream Yoga by Andrew Holecek — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Combines Western lucid dreaming techniques with the Tibetan yogas of dream and sleep.

item.title: Dream Engineering Lab — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Michelle Carr's lab at the Université de Montréal, developing sensory stimulation methods to induce lucid dreams.

item.title: Dream Catcher — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Dream journal with lucidity and clarity ratings, dream pattern statistics, nightmare tracking and reality check reminders.

item.title: Donders Sleep & Memory Lab — via awesome-lucid-dreams
item.description: Martin Dresler's lab at the Donders Institute in Nijmegen, studying the neuroscience of sleep, dreaming and lucid dreaming.
